subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What do most traditional religious teachings say about sexual relationships?
options: They are forbidden under all circumstances
They have no moral dimension at all
They should only take place within marriage
They are required of everyone before marriage
questions.explain: Many religious traditions teach that sex is best expressed within the commitment of marriage.

questions.q: What is a common misconception about religious views on same-sex relationships?
options: That denominations can differ on this issue
That some accept and some reject such relationships
That a range of views exists across and within faiths
That all religious people hold exactly the same view
questions.explain: The misconception is believing all religious people hold exactly the same view; in reality attitudes to same-sex relationships vary widely both within and between religions.

questions.q: Which of the following is commonly described as a purpose of the family in religious teaching?
options: To isolate members from wider society
To replace the need for community
To bring up children and pass on faith and values
To avoid all responsibility for others
questions.explain: Many faiths see the family as the place where children are nurtured and religious and moral values are passed on.

questions.q: What does 'celibacy' mean in a religious context?
options: Rejecting all religious belief
Abstaining from marriage and sexual relations, often for religious devotion
Having many marriages
Marrying as young as possible
questions.explain: Celibacy is the choice to abstain from marriage and sexual activity, often to focus on religious service.

questions.q: Which is commonly listed as a cause of crime?
options: Excess wealth alone
Too much education
Strong family support
Poverty, upbringing and lack of opportunity
questions.explain: Causes of crime often cited include poverty, environment, addiction and lack of opportunity.

questions.q: What does 'retribution' as an aim of punishment mean?
options: The criminal should be set free immediately
The crime should be ignored
The criminal should pay back or suffer for the wrong done
Society should commit the crime too
questions.explain: Retribution is the idea that wrongdoers deserve to be punished in proportion to their crime.

questions.q: What does the Christian idea of 'dominion' over creation traditionally mean?
options: Humans are given responsibility and authority to care for creation
Humans may destroy nature freely
Humans must never use natural resources
Nature has authority over humans
questions.explain: Dominion is often interpreted as responsible authority and care, not the right to exploit.

questions.q: Which is a non-religious (e.g. Humanist) view on the origins of the universe?
options: The universe arose through natural processes such as the Big Bang, without a creator
The universe does not exist
God personally shaped each planet
The universe was created in six literal days
questions.explain: Humanists generally explain the universe through scientific processes rather than a divine creator.

A fertility treatment helping couples conceive
An environmental policy
A type of euthanasia
questions.explain: IVF (in-vitro fertilisation) is a fertility treatment that helps couples who struggle to conceive.

questions.q: Which view best reflects a 'pro-life' position on abortion?
options: That abortion is always the woman's free choice
That the foetus is not alive at any stage
That life only begins at adulthood
That the unborn child has a right to life from conception
questions.explain: The pro-life position holds that human life begins at conception and should be protected.

questions.q: Which view on contraception is held by the Roman Catholic Church?
options: Contraception is compulsory for married couples
Artificial contraception is generally opposed, with natural family planning permitted
All forms of contraception are strongly encouraged
The Church has no teaching on the subject
questions.explain: Catholic teaching generally opposes artificial contraception while permitting natural methods of family planning.

questions.q: A common misconception about the aims of punishment is that:
options: Punishment can serve several aims at once
Protection is one possible aim
Punishment must only ever serve one single aim
Deterrence and reformation can both apply
questions.explain: In practice, a punishment can combine several aims such as deterrence, protection and reformation.
